items.stem: Why must hooks be called at the top level of a component and not inside conditions or loops?

options.text: React relies on a consistent hook call order across renders
options.rationale: Correct: hooks are matched by call order, so the order must be stable every render.
Bundle size is unrelated to the rule of hooks.

options.text: Loops are not allowed anywhere in React
options.rationale: Loops are fine in render logic; the rule is specifically about hook calls.

options.text: Hooks only work in class components
options.rationale: Hooks work in function components, not classes.

items.explanation: Correct: hooks are matched by call order, so the order must be stable every render.

items.stem: An effect that fetches data but omits a value it uses from the dependency array will most likely:

options.text: Use a stale value from an old render (stale closure)
options.rationale: Correct: omitting a used dependency captures an outdated value from the render it was created in.
It is a runtime/logic bug, not a compile error (a linter may warn).

options.text: Automatically re-run on every state change anyway
options.rationale: Omitting the dependency means it will not re-run when that value changes.
The component still renders; the data just goes stale.

items.explanation: Correct: omitting a used dependency captures an outdated value from the render it was created in.

items.stem: Which TWO are appropriate reasons to reach for useMemo or useCallback? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Avoid recomputing a genuinely expensive value each render
options.rationale: Correct: useMemo caches an expensive computation between renders.

options.text: Keep a stable reference so a memoised child does not re-render
options.rationale: Correct: useCallback stabilises a function reference for memoised children.

options.text: Wrap every value and function by default
options.rationale: Premature memoisation adds complexity and can hurt performance.

options.text: Replace the need for correct dependency arrays
options.rationale: Memoisation hooks do not remove the need for correct dependencies.

items.explanation: Correct: memoise genuinely expensive values and stabilise references for memoised children; do not memoise everything by default.
